content: To inspect the CSM performance, we use the T-distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE) BIBREF35 to reduce each high-dimensionality data point to two-dimensions via Kullback-Leibler Divergence BIBREF36. This allows us to map our character space into two-dimensions, where similar characters from our embedding space have higher probability of being mapped close by. We sampled characters from four different groups or regions. As seen in Figure FIGREF4, our learned character space effectively groups these characters, as similar characters are adjacent to one another in four regions.
